claim_scope: CPU-only static implementation and unit-test evidence; no train, validation, test_id, accuracy, or runtime promotion claim
hypothesis: A frequency-domain DG defect operator coupled to a linear correction basis can form a deterministic two-onset-frame ridge system with exact zero-correction rollback, while a precision-first LoRA interface can preserve the frozen layer exactly and reject uncompensated quantized candidates before deployment.

dg_contract.interface_operator: one-sided normal-derivative jump on Cartesian element faces
dg_contract.top_boundary: hard pressure-release projection remains external to the residual
dg_contract.cpml: left, right, and bottom exterior CPML are excluded until auxiliary-state semantics are bound

allowed: physics residuals derived from allowed inputs

precision_contract.default: full-precision frozen base plus FP32 LoRA/DoRA residual
precision_contract.quantization: optional groupwise symmetric INT8/INT4 numerical candidate only
precision_contract.quantization_compensation: SVD low-rank initialization analogous to LoftQ
precision_contract.fallback: return full-precision output whenever candidate/reference relative error exceeds the frozen tolerance

unit_gates: discrete plane wave has near-zero matched Helmholtz residual
smooth plane wave has near-zero DG normal-flux jump
linear ridge solve lowers the registered online objective
zero correction is exactly the parent
non-adjacent or more-than-two observations are rejected
full-precision LoRA zero initialization is bit-exact
quantization-error compensation strictly lowers reference output error
unsafe quantized candidate falls back to full precision
failure_signal: Any failed physics identity, future-access contract, finite check, exact rollback, LoRA identity, compensation, or fallback test rejects the core before GPU integration.
rollback: All additions are isolated. The running pretraining model, trainer, logs, latest checkpoint, and all protected checkpoint families remain untouched.
